SCOPE OF WORK The selected Service Provider shall provide housekeeping personnel for cleaning, sanitation, hygien e and other allied housekeeping activities at the office premises of the Directorate of Non-Formal & Adu lt Education, Assam, as specified in the GeM Bid/Contract. · Sweeping and cleaning of office rooms, corridors, staircases and other common areas. · Cleaning and maintenance of toilets, washrooms and sanitary facilities. · Dusting and cleaning of furniture, doors, windows, glass panels and other office fixtures. · Collection, segregation and disposal of office waste and garbage at designated places. · Cleaning and upkeep of the surrounding areas of the office premises. · Maintaining cleanliness and hygiene throughout working hours. · Any other housekeeping-related work assigned by the authorized officer of the Directorate within the a

pproved scope of work. 2. MANPOWER The Service Provider shall deploy the required number of housekeeping personnel as specified in th e GeM Bid/Contract. Personnel shall be physically fit, disciplined, properly trained and capable of perfor ming the assigned duties. Adequate manpower shall be maintained on every working day as per the ap proved requirement. 3. WORKING HOURS AND ATTENDANCE Housekeeping personnel shall attend duty during the working hours prescribed by the Directorate. Attendance shall be maintained through the attendance system/register prescribed by the Directorate. The Service Provider shall ensure punctuality and regular attendance of all deployed personnel. 4. REPLACEMENT OF PERSONNEL In case of absence of any deployed personnel, the Service Provider shall provide a suitable replace ment without delay. The Directorate may require replacement of any personnel whose conduct, perfor mance, discipline or behaviour is found unsatisfactory. Frequent withdrawal or change of personnel shal l not be made without prior intimation, except in unavoidable circumstances. 5. UNIFORM, IDENTITY CARD AND PPE The Service Provider shall provide proper uniform, identity card, gloves, masks, footwear and other necessary safety/protective equipment to all deployed personnel at its own cost. Personnel shall wear t he prescribed uniform and display identity cards while on duty. 6. STATUTORY COMPLIANCE AND LABOUR LAWS The Service Provider shall comply with all applicable Central and State Government laws, rules, noti fications and regulations relating to employment and deployment of manpower. The Service Provider s hall, as applicable, comply with provisions relating to minimum wages, EPF, ESI, bonus, wages, leave, p ayment of wages, occupational safety, social security and other statutory benefits/dues. The Service Provider shall obtain and maintain all registrations, licences and permissions required u nder applicable law, including labour-related registrations/licences wherever applicable, and shall furnis h documentary proof to the Directorate whenever required. All statutory contributions shall be deposited within the prescribed time. Any liability arising from n on-compliance with labour laws or statutory requirements shall be borne entirely by the Service Provider. No separate claim shall ordinarily be entertained from the Directorate on this account. 7. PAYMENT OF WAGES The Service Provider shall pay wages to all deployed personnel within the prescribed period and at not less than the applicable minimum wages notified by the competent authority. Payment shall preferably be made through bank transfer and documentary proof of payment shall be furnished along with the monthly bill, wherever required. Payment to the Service Provider shall be subject to satisfactory performance, certified attendance, submission of the required bill and statutory compliance documents, and availability of funds. 8. SUPERVISION The Service Provider shall nominate an authorized supervisor/contact person responsible for coordi nation with the Directorate. The supervisor shall periodically inspect the work, ensure proper deployme nt and discipline, and promptly address deficiencies pointed out by the Directorate. 9. VERIFICATION OF PERSONNEL The Service Provider shall furnish details of all personnel deployed, including name, photograph, ad dress and other identification details as required by the Directorate. Police/antecedent verification shall be ensured by the Service Provider wherever applicable. No person whose antecedents are doubtful or whose presence is considered undesirable shall be deployed. 10. SECURITY AND CONFIDENTIALITY Deployed personnel shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding official information, documents, files, records and activities noticed during duty. They shall not access, remove, copy, photograph, repro duce or disclose any official document, file, record or information without authorization. Any breach of c onfidentiality or security shall constitute a serious contractual violation and may attract appropriate act ion. 11. CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINE Personnel shall maintain proper discipline and decorum within the office premises. They shall not e ngage in misconduct, argument, unauthorized access, theft, damage to Government property, smoking , consumption of intoxicants during duty, or any activity prejudicial to the interest of the Directorate. Th e Service Provider shall be responsible for the conduct of its personnel. 12. DAMAGE/LOSS TO GOVERNMENT PROPERTY

The Service Provider shall be responsible for loss or damage to Government property caused by ne gligence, misconduct or wilful act of its personnel. The cost of such loss or damage may be recovered fr om the Service Provider after due verification. 13. PROHIBITION OF SUB-CONTRACTING The Service Provider shall not assign, transfer or sub-contract the housekeeping services to any oth er agency without prior written approval of the competent authority. The Service Provider shall remain f ully responsible for performance of the contract. 14. INSPECTION AND MONITORING The Directorate shall have the right to inspect and monitor the housekeeping services at any time d uring the contract period. The Service Provider shall comply with reasonable directions issued by the au thorized officer for improvement of services. 15. PERFORMANCE, PENALTIES AND DEDUCTIONS In case of absence of deployed personnel without suitable replacement, unsatisfactory performance , negligence, failure to perform assigned duties, non-compliance with safety requirements or other brea ch of the GeM Contract/ATC, the Directorate may impose deductions/penalties as permissible under the GeM Contract and applicable Government rules. Repeated or serious deficiencies may lead to recovery from the monthly bill, performance security or other amounts due to the Service Provider, and may also result in termination/debarment as permissi ble under applicable rules. 16. ACCIDENT, SAFETY AND INDEMNITY The Service Provider shall be solely responsible for the safety, welfare and statutory protection of it s deployed personnel while performing duties. Adequate PPE, safety instructions and safe working pract ices shall be provided. In the event of any accident, injury, death or other incident involving personnel of the Service Provid er arising out of or in connection with the performance of the services, the Service Provider shall bear al l liabilities, compensation, medical expenses, statutory dues and other obligations arising under applica ble law. The Directorate shall not be liable for employment-related claims of the Service Provider's pers onnel, except to the extent liability is imposed upon the Directorate by law. The Service Provider shall indemnify and keep indemnified the Directorate against claims, losses, d amages, penalties, expenses or liabilities arising from negligence, misconduct, statutory non-complianc e or acts/omissions of its personnel to the extent permissible under law. 17. GST AND OTHER TAXES Quoted rates shall include all applicable costs, statutory liabilities, transportation, supervision, admi nistrative expenses and incidental charges, except GST wherever separately applicable as per Governm ent rules and the GeM Contract. The Service Provider shall be responsible for timely payment of applica ble taxes and statutory dues. 18. VALIDITY OF RATES Rates quoted shall remain firm during the contract period, subject to provisions of the GeM Contract and applicable Government rules. No additional payment shall be admissible on account of increase in administrative or operational expenses except where specifically permitted under the GeM Contract or due to statutory revision expressly admissible under applicable rules. 19. CONTRACT PERIOD AND EXTENSION The contract shall remain valid for the period specified in the GeM Bid/Contract. Any extension shall be subject to satisfactory performance, availability of funds, continuing requirement and approval of the competent authority, in accordance with applicable GeM provisions. 20. ELIGIBILITY AND EXPERIENCE The bidder shall fulfil the eligibility criteria prescribed in the GeM Bid and submit all documents requ ired under the bid conditions. Where experience is prescribed, documentary evidence of satisfactory co mpletion of similar housekeeping service contracts, including work orders/agreements and performance /completion certificates, shall be furnished. The bidder shall possess valid registrations and licences required under applicable laws for providin g housekeeping/manpower services. 21. BLACKLISTING The bidder shall submit a declaration that it has not been blacklisted, debarred or banned by any C entral Government Department, State Government Department, Government undertaking, PSU or statu tory body for fraudulent, corrupt, unethical or other serious contractual misconduct. Suppression of mat erial facts or submission of false/forged documents may result in rejection of the bid and/or termination of the contract. 22. RIGHT OF THE DIRECTORATE

The Directorate reserves the right to increase or decrease the requirement of housekeeping person nel/services during the contract period, subject to the provisions of the GeM Contract, actual requireme nt and availability of funds. The Directorate also reserves the right to accept or reject any bid in accord ance with applicable GeM rules and Government instructions. 23. TERMINATION · Persistent unsatisfactory performance; · Failure to deploy the required manpower; · Repeated absenteeism or failure to provide replacement; · Violation of statutory requirements; · Misconduct, fraud or malpractice; · Breach of confidentiality or security; · Submission of false or forged documents; or · Any other material breach of contractual obligations. Termination shall be carried out in accordance with the applicable GeM terms and conditions and G overnment rules. 24. DISPUTE RESOLUTION Any dispute arising out of or in connection with the contract shall be dealt with in accordance with t he dispute resolution mechanism prescribed under the GeM General Terms and Conditions and applicab le Government rules. 25. JURISDICTION Subject to the provisions of the GeM Contract and applicable law, the courts having jurisdiction at G uwahati, Assam shall have jurisdiction over matters arising from the contract. 26. GENERAL CONDITIONS · The Service Provider shall comply with all instructions issued by the Directorate from time to time in co nnection with the housekeeping services. · The Service Provider shall not claim any additional amount for duties falling within the approved scope of work. · The Directorate shall not provide accommodation to deployed personnel, and no cooking/lodging shall b e permitted in the office premises. · All terms and conditions of the GeM General Terms and Conditions, Bid/Contract and applicable Govern ment rules shall form part of the contract. · In case of conflict between these ATC and the GeM General Terms and Conditions, the applicable provisi ons of the GeM terms shall prevail. · The Service Provider shall ensure uninterrupted and satisfactory housekeeping services throughout the contract period.
